rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

implementationCorrectness.description: Does the code actually do what it claims, handling edge cases and error paths without regressions? Score 1: logic is broken, misses obvious edge or error cases, or silently regresses existing behavior. Score 10: behaves correctly across the happy path, edge cases and failure modes, with no regressions.

rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

idiomaticity.description: Does the code follow the language, framework and project conventions a fluent reader would expect? Score 1: fights the idioms of the stack and the established patterns of the repository; reads as foreign. Score 10: indistinguishable from well-written surrounding code; uses the right idioms naturally.

rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

complexity.description: Is the solution as simple as the problem allows, without needless abstraction or convolution? Score 1: over-engineered or tangled; hard to follow, with accidental complexity that obscures intent. Score 10: minimal and clear; the simplest design that solves the problem completely.

rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

testRiskCoverage.description: Are the meaningful behaviors and risky paths exercised by tests in proportion to their risk? Score 1: risky logic ships untested; tests are absent, trivial or assert nothing useful. Score 10: risk-weighted coverage; the parts most likely to break are tested deliberately and well.

rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

documentation.description: Are non-obvious decisions, public surfaces and tricky code explained where a reader would need it? Score 1: opaque; no comments or docs where they are needed, so intent must be reverse-engineered. Score 10: just enough docs and comments to explain the why, without restating the obvious.

rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

securitySafety.description: Does the change avoid introducing vulnerabilities, leaking secrets or handling untrusted input unsafely? Score 1: introduces an exploitable flaw, leaks secrets, or trusts untrusted input unsafely. Score 10: input is validated, secrets are handled correctly, and no new attack surface is opened.

verdict.description: Binding verdict for the whole change; the CI gate reads only this field. Return fail if implementationCorrectness <= 5, or securitySafety <= 4, or any criterion <= 3; otherwise return pass.

summary.description: Markdown summary for a pull request comment: lead with the verdict, then the most important findings.
